current_bottleneck: There are two frontiers. 612a is the broad-frame IV-score frontier at 6/11 but has poor anchor-factor joint realism and a degenerate lower-clamp source-scale mechanism. 641a is the native joint scenario frontier because it preserves anchor-factor tails and IV-factor/factor-factor co-movement inside one shared rollout, but its IV coverage/location is weak.
last_result_summary: 642a compared 510a, 596a, 610a, 612a, 631a, 638a, and 641a. 641a is not best by IV count: 612a has 6/11, 610a/510a/596a have 5/11, and 641a has 4/11. But 641a is best for native IV+anchor-factor scenarios: factor KS mean 0.098, factor q99 pass 13/13, factor-factor corr shape 0.866, IV-factor corr shape 0.852. 610a/612a have poor joint factor tails and much lower generated absolute co-movement. Therefore the active target should remain 641a if the objective is a defensible joint scenario generator.
next_step_recommendation: Run a 641a evaluation-only sample-temperature sweep as the lowest-risk falsifier. It adds no architecture and tests whether the current support-valid IV failure is mostly underdispersion. If moderate temperature improves coverage/pathwise KS while preserving daily-change KS, cross-cell structure, and joint-panel factor audit, it may be disclosed as risk-policy calibration. If it fails, move to objective-level conditional density/calibration rather than more sampling knobs.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 612a is the highest IV-count native joint run at 6/11 but has a degenerate source-scale mechanism and poor anchor-factor joint audit. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product but is a composed deck, not a calibrated joint law. 641a is the clean native joint baseline because it removes post-hoc gluing and recovers strong anchor-factor realism, but it is still only 4/11 on the IV suite.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
